The government recognizes the people’s right
to be informed on matters of public safety and
security. This includes information on natural
hazards and other threats, the risks to life and
properties that they bring, and the remedies
and preparedness measures that can protect
them.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and
Management Council (NDRRMC) through the
Offi ce of Civil Defense (OCD), publishes this
Disaster Preparedness Guidebook under
the Disaster Information for Nationwide
Awareness Project. This Guidebook aims
to help people understand the true nature
of the hazards and risks they are facing and
prompt them to follow the government’s lead in
preparing for emergencies and disasters.
Moreover, local leaders are also encouraged
to use this Guidebook as reference to educate
and organize communities, schools, churches,
businesses and organizations, to bring stronger
involvement in reducing people’s vulnerabilities
and minimize the risks and threats of these
hazards.
Together, let us continue to learn and work so
that people’s lives are protected, livelihoods
are sustained, and everyone shares the fruits
of safer, climate-adaptive and disaster-resilient
communities.

REMAIN ALERT AND BE CAUTIOUS.
Wait for authorities to declare that it is safe to return

tahanan.
Use fl ashlight or emergency lamp. Be cautious in using

Maging maingat sa paggamit ng kandila o gasera.
AFTER
Throw away rainwater in cans, pots and tires to prevent

Stay away from fallen trees, damaged structures and

Be cautious in checking and repairing the damaged

Do not go sightseeing as you may hinder the work of
the emergency services. Huwag gumala upang hindi maabala

Stay away from glass windows. Umiwas sa mga salaming
bintana.
Check for wet or submerged electrical outlets and
appliances before turning on electricity. Siguraduhing
walang basa o nakababad na outlet o kagamitan bago buksan ang linya
ng kuryente.
MONITOR THE NEWS FOR WEATHER UPDATES.
STAY ALERT AND STAY TUNED
Tropical cyclone is an extreme weather condition
characterized by large scale circulation of strong winds,
low atmospheric pressure and heavy rains. It can cause
fl ooding, storm surge, landslides and fl ash fl oods.
Ang bagyo ay isang uri ng lagay ng panahon na nagdudulot ng malalakas
at mabilis na hangin at pag-ulan na maaaring maging sanhi ng matitinding
pagbaha, daluyong ng dagat at pagguho ng mga lupa.
BEFORE
Know the early warning and evacuation plan of the
community. Alamin ang plano ng komunidad sa pagbibigay-babala
at paglikas.
Check the integrity of your house and repair weak parts.
Suriin ang bahay at kumpunihin ang mga mahina o sirang bahagi nito.
Prepare your family’s GO BAG containing items
needed for survival. Ihanda ang GO BAG na naglalaman ng mga
pangangailangan ng pamilya.
When notifi ed, immediately go to the designated
evacuation center. Kapag inabisuhan ng kinauukulan, mabilis na
lumikas sa itinakdang evacuation center.
DURING
Put livestock and pets in a safe area or designated
evacuation site for animals. Ilikas ang mga alagang hayop sa
ligtas na lugar.
Stay calm. Stay indoors and tune in for latest news and
weather updates. Manatiling mahinahon. Manatili sa loob ng bahay o
evacuation center at makinig sa pinakabagong balita at taya ng panahon.
Monitor the news for weather updates, warnings and
advisories. Alamin ang balita ukol sa panahon at mga anunsyong

STAY IN A SAFE AREA AND BE ALERT.
A landslide is the movement of soil, rocks, mud or
debris down a slope. This can be caused by continuous
heavy rains (rain-induced landslides) or shaking due to
earthquake (earthquake-induced landslides).
Ang landslide o pagguho ay ang pagbaba ng lupa, bato, putik at iba pang
bagay mula sa mataas na lugar. Ito ay maaaring mangyari kapag may
malakas at tuloy-tuloy na pag-ulan o pagyanig mula sa lindol.

WHEN YOU ARE OUTSIDE, MOVE TO AN OPEN AREA!
If you’re in a moving vehicle, stop and exit the vehicle.
Kapag nagmamaneho, itabi at ihinto ang sasakyan at lumabas.

An earthquake is the weak to violent shaking of the
ground produced by sudden movement of rock materials
below the earth’s surface.
Ang lindol ay ang pagyanig ng lupa dahil sa biglaang paggalaw ng mga

Scrape the accumulated ash in roofs to prevent collapse.

A volcanic eruption occurs when hot materials such

Ang pagputok ng bulkan ay nangyayari kapag nagbubuga ang bulkan ng

V O L C A N I C E R U P T I O N
IN CASE OF FIRE
Sound the fi re alarm and call 911 for assistance. Patunugin
ang fi re alarm at tumawag sa 911 para sa kagyat na tulong.
If you’re in a building, use the stairs and do not use
elevators. Kung nasa loob ng isang gusali, gumamit ng hagdan sa
paglikas. Huwag gumamit ng elevator.
After the fi re, do not return inside your house or building
unless authorities deemed it safe. Pagkatapos ng sunog,
huwag bumalik sa loob ng bahay o gusali hangga’t wala pang abiso ang
kinauukulan.
Have yourself checked for injuries. Ipasuri ang sarili kung
nasugatan o nasaktan.
If there is smoke, get down low and cover your mouth
and nose with damp cloth. Kapag may makapal na usok,
gumapang papuntang ligtas na lugar. Takpan ang bibig at ilong ng basang
tela o damit.
If your clothes catch fi re, STOP running, DROP to the
fl oor, and ROLL to put out the fl ames. Kapag umapoy ang
damit na suot, tumigil sa pagtakbo, dumapa at magpagulong-gulong
hanggang maapula ang apoy.
If trapped, stay in the room and signal for help using
bright colored cloth at the window or make noise. Kapag
hindi makalabas, manatili sa loob at humingi ng tulong gamit ang tela
na may matingkad na kulay o gumawa ng ingay para marining ng mga
rescuers.
Before opening doors, check handle fi rst. If hot, DO NOT
OPEN as the room may already be on fi re. Bago buksan ang
anumang pinto, pakiramdaman muna kung ito ay maiinit. Huwag buksan
kung ito ay maiinit dahil maaaring may sunog na sa loob nito.
Stay calm and evacuate immediately. Manatiling mahinahon
at agad lumikas.
Uncontrolled fi re poses danger not only to human
life but also to people’s investments, properties and
livelihood. Basic knowledge on fi re prevention and on
what to do in case of fi re is very important. Ang sunog ay
mga bantang panganib sa kaligtasan ng tao at sa kanyang ari-arian at
kabuhayan. Mahalaga na may kaalaman ukol sa pag-iwas sa sunog at
mga dapat gawin sakaling magkasunog.
FIRE PREVENTION
Befriend a fi reman. Makipagkaibigan sa bumbero.
Hire an electrician to check on your electrical wirings
at least once a year. Ipasuri sa electrician ang koneksyon ng mga
kuryente taon taon.
Unplug appliances and gadgets after using or charging.
Tanggalin sa pagkakasaksak ng mga gamit matapos itong gamitin.
DO NOT leave lighted candles and cigarettes unattended.
Huwag pabayaan ang mga nakasinding kandila o sigarilyo.
Teach children on fi re safety. Turuan ang mga kabataan ukol sa
kaligtasan sa sunog.
Learn how to use a fi re extinguisher. Remember PASS:
Pull the pin, Aim the noozle at the base of fi re, Squeeze
the lever, and Sweep from side to side. Alamin ang paggamit
ng fi re extinguisher: hilahin ang ‘pin’, itapat ang hose sa pinagmumulan
ng apoy, diinan ang pindutan, at galawin ang hose na parang winawalis
ang apoy.
Turn off LPG tanks when not in use. Isara ang LPG kapag
hindi ginagamit.
Practice your evacuation plan and participate in fi re
drills. Sanayin ang sarili at mga kasamahan sa evacuation plan at
sumali sa mga fi re drills.
Ensure that fi re alarms and sprinklers work. Siguraduhing
gumagana ang mga fi re alarms at sprinklers.
F I R E
First aid kit with remedies for fever, LBM, minor wounds
and pain, and maintenance medicines. First aid kit, kasama
ang panlunas sa lagnat, LBM, sugat at iba pa, at mga gamot na regular
na iniinom ng kapamilya.
Spare cash including coins. Pera at barya.
Easy-to-serve, ready-to-eat food enough for three days.
Pagkain na madaling ihanda, di na kailangang lutuin, at sapat para sa
tatlong araw.
Drinking water in sealed containers enough for three
days. Inuming tubig sa saradong lalagyan at sapat para sa tatlong araw.
Mobile phones, powerbanks and chargers. Telepono,
powerbank at charger.
Ropes, old newspaper and ecobags made of strong
materials. Lubid, lumang dyaryo at matitibay na lalagyan.
Clothing, raincoat, boots and sanitary supplies. Damit,
kapote, botas at mga sanitary supplies.
Sleeping bags or mats, and blankets. Banig at kumot.
Items for special needs of young and older members
of the family, including persons with disabilities. Mga
gamit para sa pangangailangan ng mga sanggol, bata, matatanda at may
kapansanan.
REMEMBER THESE THREE IMPORTANT GUIDES.
THE GO BAG CONTAINS IMPORTANT ITEMS NEEDED
BY THE FAMILY TO SURVIVE.
The GO BAG should be stored properly where it can be
easily accessed in case of an emergency. Ilagay ang GO
BAG sa lugar na madali itong makita at makuha sa oras ng sakuna.
Important
documents
in
waterproof
container.
Mahahalagang dokumento sa selyadong lalagyan.
Flashlight, candles, matches and whistle. Flashlight, kandila,
posporo at silbato.
Radio with fresh and extra batteries. Radyo na may bago at
ekstrang baterya.
The GO BAG items should be checked and replenished
every three months. Suriin ang laman ng GO BAG kada tatlong
buwan at palitan ang mga laman nito na malapit ng masira.
When there is an impending danger, we need to leave
our homes and evacuate to safer areas. To prepare for
these emergencies, we should have a ready GO BAG
that we can bring along immediately. Kapag may mga banta
ng panganib, kailangan lumikas papunta sa higit na ligtas na lugar. Bilang
paghahanda sa mga ganitong pagkakataon, mahalaga na may GO BAG
na dadalhin ang pamilya.
Coordinate with leaders on community evacuation plan.
Decide with the family on where to meet in case there
is a need to evacuate. Makipag-ugnayan sa mga lider para sa
plano sa paglikas ng komunidad. Pag-usapan din sa pamilya kung saan
tutungo sa oras na kailangang lumikas.

Community Leaders’ Guide
1. CREATE A TEAM. Recruit or assign people with similar interests
and commitment towards making the community safe. Mag-
recruit o magtalaga ng mga tao na may katulad na interes sa pagbuo ng ligtas na
komunidad.
2. IDENTIFY HAZARDS, RISKS AND RESOURCES. Identify
all hazards and threats to the community and the available
resources which can be tapped to prepare for these hazards.
Alamin ang mga bantang panganib sa komunidad at ang mga maaaring maggamit
upang paghandaan ang mga ito.
3. PLAN YOUR ACTIONS. Set outcome-based goals and plan
the activities geared towards these goals. Itakda ang mga layunin at
planuhin ang mga aktibidad na nakatuon sa mga layuning ito.
4. STUDY, EDUCATE AND EXERCISE. Study best practices of other
communities. Educate members of the community through
Project DINA videos and publications. Organize disaster
preparedness and response exercises and drills. Pag-aralan ang
mga kasanayan ng ibang mga komunidad. Turuan ang mga miyembro ng komunidad
sa pamamagitan ng mga video at publikasyon ng Project DINA. Magtakda ng mga
pagsasanay sa kahandaan at pagtugon sa sakuna.
5. CULTIVATE VIGILANCE. Nurture community resilience by
staying vigilant especially when hazards threaten the community.
Monitor the situation, coordinate with local authorities, and
disseminate safety and evacuation orders on time. Panatilihin ang
katatagan ng komunidad at maging mapagbantay lalo na kapag pagbabanta ng
mga panganib. Subaybayan ang sitwasyon, makipag-ugnayan sa mga lokal na
awtoridad, at ipamahagi ang mga lkautusang pangkaligtasan at paglikas sa tamang
oras.
Local offi cials which include school authorities and offi ce managers
can provide the needed leadership through well-planned activities
geared towards building community resilience. The following
tips can help guide leaders in keeping the community safe and
ready in case of emergencies and disasters. Ang mga lokal na opisyal
kasama ang mga tagapamahala ng mga paaralan at opisina ay maaaring mamuno sa
pamamagitan nang mahusay na pagpaplano na mga gawain na nakatuon sa pagbuo
ng handang komunidad. Ang mga sumusunod na gabay ay makatutulong sa mga lider
pagpapanatiling ligtas at handa ang mga komunidad.
